paragraphs: Here's the lesson, friend. The people asked for a lighter load, and the elders who had served Solomon said kind words would make them his servants "forever" (2 Chronicles 10:7). Rehoboam had wisdom sitting right there in the room and he rejected it (2 Chronicles 10:8). Good advice does no good if you won't take it, and I've stared at a recipe card and still done my own thing, so I'm talking to myself too.

Notice who Rehoboam listened to, though. The young men had grown up with him, so they sounded familiar and they sounded bold (2 Chronicles 10:9-11). But bold and wise are NOT the same thing, friend. When you're deciding something big, ask who gives you advice and what they want you to become, because the loudest voice in the room is not always the wisest one.

And here's the part that steadies me. The text says this turn of events was from God, so that the LORD might fulfill the word He had spoken through Ahijah to Jeroboam (2 Chronicles 10:15). So a harsh king and a split kingdom did not catch God off guard. When things fall apart around you, His word still stands, and that's something you can build on. Rehoboam's story isn't over, and neither is the lesson.
